correctness.rationale: Dividing by gcd gives primitive two-supported legs; parity forces support {2,q}; coprimality and the factorization (q^b-1)(q^b+1)=2^(a+1) yield only (q,b,a)=(3,1,2), so the exponent graph is exactly (2,-1) edges. Diagonal lattice slices are paths. Sum of path independence numbers, their optimizer counts, and exact coefficient-parity enumeration prove the formulas for every positive R,S and n. Direct exact arithmetic tests of all 90 small boxes, 120 formula cutoffs and four exhaustive independent-set checks passed; these are corroboration, not the general proof.

value.rationale: The recent high-rank extremal Pythagorean-pair problem motivates the smallest nontrivial fixed support. This theorem determines its complete exact invariant for all prime pairs and rectangular cutoffs, not an arbitrary small numerical slice. The unique {2,3} support produces a qualitative half-density/whole-density discontinuity, while the path decomposition also specifies every optimizer. These consequences are not implied by the source asymptotic inequalities, and form a reusable exact boundary model for higher-rank study.
